question: Does an unmodified stock node accept a frame built entirely by our encoder?
why_this_direction: TESTING.md: a decoder that is merely lenient passes every inbound test while emitting frames nobody accepts. This is the direction that fails in the field, and the only one that proves interoperability.

setup.transmitter: Heltec V3 running our own SX1262 driver; the host supplied the frame bytes verbatim, the firmware interprets nothing
setup.frame_built_by: tethermesh: header::encode, channel::channel_hash, crypto::expand_psk + ctr_apply + nonce, message::Data::encode, frame::encode
setup.judge: Heltec V3, unmodified Meshtastic 2.7.26.54e0d8d, US/LongFast, default channel

stock_node_log: [RadioIf] Lora RX (id=0x0badc0de fr=0x7e570001 to=0xffffffff, HopLim=3 Ch=0x8 encrypted len=44 rxSNR=6.25)
[Router] Received text msg from=0x7e570001, id=0xbadc0de, msg=tethermesh-conformance-1
what_this_proves_simultaneously: 16-byte header layout, field order and little-endian encoding
flag bit packing for hop_limit and hop_start
channel hash function and its use of the modem preset name
PSK short-index expansion to the default channel key
AES-128 key schedule and the CTR keystream
the nonce construction and its byte order
protobuf Data encoding, including proto3 default omission
frame assembly and the header/ciphertext boundary
sync word and LongFast modem parameters on the transmit side
not_yet_proven: direct messages under PKI (channel-encrypted direct messages work; the X25519 path is untested)

nodeinfo.question: Does a stock node parse our User record and list us as a peer?
nodeinfo.note: The macaddr field is deprecated since 2.1.x and still emitted by 2.7.26; it was included because a stock node emits it, and byte-level agreement is decided by the wire rather than by the schema.

traceroute.question: Does a stock node answer a direct request from us, and can we read its reply?
traceroute.request: addressed to 0x3369e764 (not broadcast), Data{portnum=70 TRACEROUTE_APP, payload empty, want_response=true}
their_log: [Router] Received traceroute from=0x7e570001, id=0xbadd002, portnum=70, payloadlen=0
[Router] Send response (id=0x6d826bc5 fr=0x3369e764 to=0x7e570001, HopLim=2 Portnum=70)
traceroute.verdict: ANSWERED, AND WE DECRYPTED THE ANSWER
traceroute.note: A repeated (from, id) is silently dropped by their duplicate suppression — the same behaviour history.rs implements, observed from the far side. A rerun with a stale id looks identical to a frame that never arrived, which is why the id is overridable.

interoperability_gate.source: PLAN.md: a physical, unmodified device must show our node, render our text, accept a direct message, and list us in a route trace
interoperability_gate.accept a direct message: DONE for channel encryption — an addressed, non-broadcast packet was accepted and answered; PKI untested
interoperability_gate.list us in a route trace: DONE — traceroute answered with our request_id and an SNR reading
